Full huge phylogenetic tree
```{r}
# Start with a clean slate
rm(list = ls())

# GTDB-Tk phylogenetic placement figure
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)

# Read GTDB-Tk outputs
tree <- read.tree(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/metabolic_output/339genus/gtdbtk_Genome_files/classify/gtdbtk.backbone.bac120.classify.tree"
)

gtdb <- read.delim(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/metabolic_output/339genus/gtdbtk_Genome_files/classify/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv",
  sep = "\t",
  header = TRUE,
  check.names = FALSE
)


# Extract taxonomy from GTDB classification
taxonomy <- gtdb %>%
  select(user_genome, user_genome, classification) %>%
  separate(
    classification,
    into = c(
      "domain",
      "phylum",
      "class",
      "order",
      "family",
      "genus",
      "species"
    ),
    sep = ";",
    fill = "right"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    domain  = str_remove(domain,  "^d__"),
    phylum  = str_remove(phylum,  "^p__"),
    class   = str_remove(class,   "^c__"),
    order   = str_remove(order,   "^o__"),
    family  = str_remove(family,  "^f__"),
    genus   = str_remove(genus,   "^g__"),
    species = str_remove(species, "^s__")
  )

# Use GTDB names to match to the GTDB tree
mag_ids <- taxonomy$user_genome

# Verify that all MAGs occur in the GTDB placement tree
sum(mag_ids %in% tree$tip.label)
length(mag_ids)

setdiff(mag_ids, tree$tip.label)


# Create annotation dataframe for every tree tip
tip_data <- data.frame(
  label = tree$tip.label,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  left_join(
    taxonomy,
    by = c("label" = "user_genome")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    genome_type = if_else(
      label %in% mag_ids,
      "MAG",
      "GTDB reference"
    )
  )

# Plot the full GTDB backbone
# NOTE: full tree still uses original GTDB tip names internally,
# which is fine because we are only using this as a QC/reference plot.
p <- ggtree(
  tree,
  layout = "circular",
  linewidth = 0.15
) %<+% tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(
    data = function(x) dplyr::filter(x, label %in% mag_ids),
    aes(color = phylum),
    size = 1.6
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actinomycetota"   = "#7c6f64",
      "Bacteroidota"     = "#5b7694",
      "Cyanobacteriota"  = "#52796f",
      "Pseudomonadota"   = "#b45f5a",
  "Chloroflexota"   = "#C49A56"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right"
  )

p

# Output directory
out_dir <- "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/phylo_tree"

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "full_phylotree.png"),
  plot = p,
  width = 10,
  height = 10,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)

# PDF version
ggsave(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/pdf_figs/FigS5.pdf",
  plot = p,
  device = cairo_pdf,
  width = 10,
  height = 10,
  units = "in"
)

```


Prune tree
```{r}
# PRUNE TREE TO MAGs AND RENAME TIPS FOR FIGURE / iTOL

# Keep only our MAGs using ORIGINAL GTDB names
mag_tree <- keep.tip(tree, mag_ids)

# Check that the pruned tree contains all 339 MAGs
Ntip(mag_tree)


# Create annotation dataframe that matches the SHORTENED tree labels
mag_tip_data <- taxonomy %>%
  transmute(
    label = user_genome,
    domain,
    phylum,
    class,
    order,
    family,
    genus,
    species
  )

# Confirm every tree tip matches annotation data
sum(mag_tree$tip.label %in% mag_tip_data$label)


# Plot circular MAG-only tree
p_mag <- ggtree(
  mag_tree,
  layout = "circular",
  linewidth = 0.4
) %<+% mag_tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(
    aes(color = phylum),
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actinomycetota"   = "#7c6f64",
      "Bacteroidota"     = "#5b7694",
      "Cyanobacteriota"  = "#52796f",
      "Pseudomonadota"   = "#b45f5a",
  "Chloroflexota"   = "#C49A56"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right"
  )

p_mag

# Plot rectangular MAG-only tree
p_mag_rect <- ggtree(
  mag_tree,
  layout = "rectangular",
  linewidth = 0.4
) %<+% mag_tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(
    aes(color = phylum),
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Actinomycetota"   = "#7c6f64",
      "Bacteroidota"     = "#5b7694",
      "Cyanobacteriota"  = "#52796f",
      "Pseudomonadota"   = "#b45f5a",
  "Chloroflexota"   = "#C49A56"
    )
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right"
  )

p_mag_rect



```



Exports for iTOL
```{r}

# Export the MAG-only tree for iTOL
# THIS FILE WILL CONTAIN THE SHORTENED TIP NAMES
write.tree(
  mag_tree,
  file = "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/phylo_tree/MAG_339_GTDB_placement.tree"
)

# Create iTOL phylum annotation file

# Choose colors for each phylum
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Actinomycetota"   = "#7c6f64",
      "Bacteroidota"     = "#5b7694",
      "Cyanobacteriota"  = "#52796f",
      "Pseudomonadota"   = "#b45f5a",
  "Chloroflexota"   = "#C49A56"
)

# Build annotation table using tree names
itol_phylum <- taxonomy %>%
  select(user_genome, phylum) %>%
  mutate(
    color = phylum_colors[phylum]
  )

# Check that every MAG received a color
itol_phylum %>%
  filter(is.na(color))

# Should return 0 rows

# Write iTOL DATASET_COLORSTRIP file
phylum_file <- "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/phylo_tree/iTOL_phylum_colorstrip.txt"



# CREATE iTOL DISPLAY LABELS:
# Genus + MAG ID

label_file <- paste0(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/",
  "phylo_tree/iTOL_MAG_labels_339.txt"
)

# Create labels
itol_labels <- taxonomy %>%
  transmute(
    ID = user_genome,
    DISPLAY_LABEL = ifelse(
      is.na(genus) | genus == "",
      paste0("Unassigned | ", user_genome),
      paste0(genus, " | ", user_genome)
    )
  )

# Inspect before exporting
print(itol_labels)

# Write iTOL LABELS file
cat(
  "LABELS\n",
  "SEPARATOR TAB\n",
  "DATA\n",
  sep = "",
  file = label_file
)

write.table(
  itol_labels,
  file = label_file,
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = FALSE,
  append = TRUE
)
```

Metabolic functions for iTOL
```{r}

# Read METABOLIC MW-score input table

metabolic_file <- paste0(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/metabolic_output/",
  "339genus/MW-score_result_table_input.txt"
)

mw_input <- read.delim(
  metabolic_file,
  sep = "\t",
  header = TRUE,
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Inspect structure
colnames(mw_input)
head(mw_input)



# Convert Func1 and Func2 into one MAG x function table
#
# Each row of the original file contains a pair of metabolic
# functions. Extract each individual function occurring in
# either Func1 or Func2 for each MAG.


metabolic_long <- mw_input %>%
  select(
    user_genome = `#Genome`,
    Func1,
    Func2
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Func1, Func2),
    names_to = "function_source",
    values_to = "METABOLIC_function"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(METABOLIC_function),
    METABOLIC_function != ""
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    user_genome,
    METABOLIC_function
  )




# Parse METABOLIC function codes and create SHORT labels
#
# Example:
#
# Original:
# C-S-01:Organic carbon oxidation - CO oxidation
#
# Becomes:
# Function_code = C-S-01
# Function       = Organic carbon oxidation - CO oxidation
# display_name   = CO oxidation
#
# Full METABOLIC names are retained in "Function".
# Only "display_name" is used in iTOL.


metabolic_long <- metabolic_long %>%
  mutate(

    # METABOLIC function code
    Function_code = str_extract(
      METABOLIC_function,
      "^[CNSO]-S-[0-9]+"
    ),

    # Full function name
    Function = str_remove(
      METABOLIC_function,
      "^[CNSO]-S-[0-9]+:"
    ) %>%
      str_remove(":$") %>%
      str_squish(),

    # First letter identifies METABOLIC cycle
    Cycle_code = str_sub(
      Function_code,
      1,
      1
    ),

 
    # Short publication-friendly name for iTOL

    display_name = Function %>%

      # Remove redundant parent pathway descriptions
      str_remove("^Organic carbon oxidation - ") %>%
      str_remove("^Carbon fixation - ") %>%

      # Put gene/system identifiers in parentheses
      str_replace(
        "^Nitrate reduction - (.+)$",
        "Nitrate reduction (\\1)"
      ) %>%
      str_replace(
        "^Nitrite reduction - (.+)$",
        "Nitrite reduction (\\1)"
      ) %>%
      str_replace(
        "^Nitrite ammonification - (.+)$",
        "Nitrite ammonification (\\1)"
      ) %>%
      str_replace(
        "^Sulfide oxidation - (.+)$",
        "Sulfide oxidation (\\1)"
      ) %>%
      str_replace(
        "^Sulfur oxidation - (.+)$",
        "Sulfur oxidation (\\1)"
      ) %>%
      str_replace(
        "^Sulfite reduction - (.+)$",
        "Sulfite reduction (\\1)"
      ) %>%

      # Remove trailing punctuation / extra spaces
      str_remove(":$") %>%
      str_squish()
  )


# Assign METABOLIC biogeochemical cycle
#
# C = Carbon
# N = Nitrogen
# S = Sulfur
# O = Other
#
# METABOLIC assigns:
# O-S-01 = Iron reduction
# O-S-02 = Iron oxidation
#
# We display those two separately as "Iron" to match the
# metabolic-cycle figure used in the manuscript.

metabolic_long <- metabolic_long %>%
  mutate(
    Cycle = case_when(

      Cycle_code == "C" ~ "Carbon",

      Cycle_code == "N" ~ "Nitrogen",

      Cycle_code == "S" ~ "Sulfur",

      Function_code %in% c(
        "O-S-01",
        "O-S-02"
      ) ~ "Iron",

      Cycle_code == "O" ~ "Other",

      TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
    )
  )



# Create definitive function classification table
function_classification <- metabolic_long %>%
  distinct(
    Function_code,
    Function,
    display_name,
    Cycle
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Cycle = factor(
      Cycle,
      levels = c(
        "Carbon",
        "Nitrogen",
        "Sulfur",
        "Iron",
        "Other",
        "Unclassified"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Cycle,
    Function_code,
    Function
  )

print(
  function_classification,
  n = Inf
)


# Number of functions in each cycle
function_classification %>%
  count(Cycle)


# Inspect Iron and Other functions
function_classification %>%
  filter(
    Cycle %in% c("Iron", "Other")
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)


# Check that shortened labels remain unique
#
# IMPORTANT:
# Shortening names could theoretically cause two different
# functions to receive the same display name.
duplicate_display_names <- function_classification %>%
  count(display_name) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(
  duplicate_display_names,
  n = Inf
)

# Ideally: 0 rows


#Calculate prevalence of each function across MAGs
function_prevalence <- metabolic_long %>%
  distinct(
    user_genome,
    Function_code,
    Function,
    display_name,
    Cycle
  ) %>%
  count(
    Function_code,
    Function,
    display_name,
    Cycle,
    name = "n_MAGs"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    percent_MAGs =
      100 * n_MAGs /
      n_distinct(metabolic_long$user_genome)
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Cycle,
    desc(n_MAGs)
  )

print(
  function_prevalence,
  n = Inf
)



# Convert to MAG x function presence/absence
#
# If a MAG/function combination occurs in the MW-score input,
# it receives a 1. Missing combinations will later become 0.

metabolic_binary_long <- metabolic_long %>%
  distinct(
    user_genome,
    Function_code,
    Function,
    display_name,
    Cycle
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    presence_binary = 1L
  )


# Establish function order for iTOL
#
# Carbon -> Nitrogen -> Sulfur -> Iron -> Other
function_classification <- function_classification %>%
  filter(
    Cycle != "Unclassified"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Cycle = factor(
      Cycle,
      levels = c(
        "Carbon",
        "Nitrogen",
        "Sulfur",
        "Iron",
        "Other"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    Cycle,
    Function_code,
    Function
  )


# These are the SHORT labels that will appear in iTOL
function_names <- function_classification$display_name


# Make MAG x metabolic-function matrix

itol_metabolic_matrix <- metabolic_binary_long %>%
  filter(
    Cycle != "Unclassified"
  ) %>%
  select(
    user_genome,
    display_name,
    presence_binary
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = user_genome,
    names_from = display_name,
    values_from = presence_binary,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  select(
    user_genome,
    all_of(function_names)
  )


# Define colors
# Same general color scheme as manuscript metabolic figure.

cycle_colors <- c(
  "Carbon"   = "#d6a85f",
  "Nitrogen" = "#a88bc2",
  "Sulfur"   = "#d98c73",
  "Iron"     = "#81a6a1",
  "Other"    = "#b8b8b8"
)

# Match each function to its cycle color
field_colors <- function_classification %>%
  mutate(
    color = cycle_colors[
      as.character(Cycle)
    ]
  )


# Make sure every function received a color
stopifnot(
  !any(
    is.na(field_colors$color)
  )
)



# Write iTOL binary annotation file

itol_file <- paste0(
  "D:/Planktothrix_microbiomes/manuscript_figures/",
  "phylo_tree/iTOL_metabolic_binary.txt"
)

cat(
  "DATASET_BINARY\n",
  "SEPARATOR TAB\n",
  "DATASET_LABEL\tMetabolic functions\n",
  "COLOR\t#000000\n",

  "FIELD_LABELS\t",
  paste(
    function_names,
    collapse = "\t"
  ),
  "\n",

  "FIELD_SHAPES\t",
  paste(
    rep(
      1,
      length(function_names)
    ),
    collapse = "\t"
  ),
  "\n",

  "FIELD_COLORS\t",
  paste(
    field_colors$color,
    collapse = "\t"
  ),
  "\n",

  "DATA\n",
  sep = "",
  file = itol_file
)



# Append MAG presence/absence data to iTOL file

write.table(
  itol_metabolic_matrix,
  file = itol_file,
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = FALSE,
  append = TRUE
)
```
